answer: Koalas eat almost nothing but eucalyptus leaves. Now and then they eat leaves from other trees, such as Melaleuca or pine, but only in small amounts [1]. Australia has nearly 900 kinds of eucalyptus, and koalas have been recorded eating about 70 of them. The ones they choose depend on the region, the season and the individual koala [1][2]. An adult eats about 600–800 g of leaves a day (roughly 1.5 lb), sometimes with soft stems, flowers or bark. Their very long gut and a large caecum full of microbes let them digest the tough, toxic leaves [1]. The leaves have little nutrition, so koalas save energy by sleeping for most of the day and feeding in the evening [2]. They rarely drink, because they get most of their water from the leaves [1][2].
